title: Normalized ordinary comparison data for sheaf slices
statement: For small sites $(C,J),(D,K)$ [def-weil-size-convention], commutative ring sheaves $R_X,R_Y$, a ringed-topos morphism $f$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], and a target sheaf $A$, define the ordinary comparison data as follows. Choose the element-site slice presentations [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction], normalized so that restriction of $A\times F$ to its fibre over $a$ is the second projection. Specify the arrowwise slice inverse image, the product comparison, its induced set-localization square, and the restriction of the structural ring map. Specify module pullbacks by their adjunctions to the given induced direct images; give inverse and direct-image comparison isomorphisms which are mates, fixing the underlying direct-image comparison to the geometric mate. Finally record exact additive restrictions, their preservation of K-injective complexes, and preservation of K-flat complexes with flat terms. These are precisely the unchanged structures SheafSliceSetLocalization and RingedSheafSliceOrdinaryComparison; sheafSliceUnderlyingRestriction is the identity identification of forgetting and restriction. The auxiliary structure RingedSheafSliceSquare records only the geometric and ordinary module square fields, before the restriction exactness and resolution preservation fields.

proof.text: Use the existing sectionwise element restriction for the underlying identity. Record the fibre normalization, geometric square, module mate identities, exactness and resolution preservation as fields. This moves the existing ordinary interfaces without changing any field or its meaning.
